# Supercharger (factory and aftermarket)

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Remove intake manifold, install throttle body and blower with bypass valve, then fit adapter and fuel rail. [t1326]

[Partial] Install a Cummins R2.8 diesel engine, then perform an extensive modification to fit it through the firewall. [t1884]

[Partial] Install a supercharger system including intake components and swap to an engine control module. [t1501]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Gather a working throttle body along with its cable.
2. Secure an extra MAF sensor as a backup component.
3. Install a brake booster line that may have a different shape or valve location than stock.
4. Connect the intake tube running from the throttle to the blower, including all tubing underneath for vacuum and coolant hoses.
5. Attach a PCV valve and hose to the passenger side of the SC engine's valve cover.
6. Mount the supercharger blower unit along with its attached bypass valve.
7. Fit an intake adapter into place.
8. Install the fuel rail, ensuring all injectors are attached with their o-rings and plastic spacers included.
9. Place the intake manifold over the engine heads.
10. [Partial] Connect a boost control solenoid to manage pressure regulation.
11. Mount a pulley bridge designed for both AC and blower operation plus its belt if it appears sound.
12. Attach an A/C compressor unit to the assembly.
13. Secure a harmonic balancer, preferably with six ribs if upgrading pulleys or using a solid coupler.
14. [Partial] Swap in the engine control module (ECM), recommending the SC version for better fuel mapping under boost.
15. Inspect all intake bolts carefully before tightening them in three phases: finger tight, half specification, and full specification.

_Procedure reported by [t1501]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1326] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Remove the intake manifold to access the engine components.
2. Install a new throttle body with its cable and MAF sensor for backup support.
3. Connect the brake booster line, noting that it may have a different shape or valve location than stock.
4. Route an intake tube from the throttle body to the blower, including all connected vacuum and coolant hoses underneath.
5. Install the PCV valve on the passenger side of the valve cover (or fabricate a two-piece tubing line if pulling the cover).
6. Mount the supercharger blower with its attached bypass valve.
7. Fit an intake adapter to connect the throttle tube to the blower outlet.
8. Swap in the fuel rail and injectors, ensuring all small O-rings and plastic spacers are included.
9. Install a boost control solenoid (BCS) if desired for better regulation of the bypass valve.

</details>

## Parts

- [Partial] A/C Compressor: 6-rib pulley recommended for solid couplers [t1501]
- Blower with bypass valve [t1326]
- ECM, Engine Control Module: SC-specific preferred for boost mapping; NA acceptable but may run rich. [t1501]
- Fuel rail and injectors [t1326, t1501]
- [Partial] Harmonic Balancer: Matched to blower pulley size [t1501]
- Intake adapter [t1326]
- Intake Manifold [t1501]
- Intake tube [t1326]
- PCV valve or tubing line [t1326]
- Supercharger Blower: Factory or rebuilt, e.g., from Cobalt SS donor [t1501]
- [Partial] Throttle body: With cable [t1326]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Polish the cylinder heads while they are off for a better finish. [t1326]
- [Partial] Replace the knock sensor during disassembly if needed. [t1326]
- [Partial] Consider adding headers to improve flow. [t1326]
- Use a UHMWPE intake spacer on an NA motor, modified slightly to fit the SC pattern. [t1501]
- Inspect all pulled bolts carefully as some yield during installation and risk breaking off in the manifold. [t1501]
- Tighten fasteners in three phases: finger tight, half spec, then full spec. [t1501]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Losing engine timing by failing to clock the motor to TDC before removing the distributor (dizzy). [t1501]
- [Partial] Running a rich idle with an NA ECM during stop-and-go driving without swapping in the SC unit. [t1501]
- Over-widening the blower outlet port, which can result in lost boost pressure. [t1501]
